tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SearchPlugins
tools.description:
Search the user's claude.ai plugin catalog by keyword. Call this when a plugin (slash command, skill bundle, hook, or agent) from the user's org catalog might help complete the task. The user does not need to name a plugin: search when the task depends on their team's own process, systems or data and nothing you already have, the project's own scripts included, covers it.

Examples:
- "use the deploy plugin" → keywords ["deploy"]
- "is there something for linting?" → keywords ["lint", "format", "code quality"]
- "ship this to staging" → keywords ["deploy", "release", "staging"]
- "review this contract against our playbook" → keywords ["legal", "contract", "playbook"]
- "which deals close this week?" → keywords ["sales", "pipeline", "crm"]

Do not search unasked for one-off questions or tasks you can handle directly ("explain this regex", "fix this typo"), or after the user ignored a suggestion in this conversation.

Returns a ranked list with id, name, description, and whether the plugin is already enabled for this session (in a channel session, whether the channel has it). When results fit and SuggestPluginInstall is among your tools, call it to render the install card; otherwise relay the relevant results in text instead. If nothing relevant, proceed without mentioning that you searched.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.description:

tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation

### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3

- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

| A-5 | 1 | Four I3-closure transitions extend the §5.4 table: REPRODUCED→ESCALATED (no suspect), ATTRIBUTED→ESCALATED (zero budget), SHIPPED→ESCALATED (merge blocked), CANARY→ESCALATED (revert failed or re-entry limit). | A-6 | 1 | RETIRED is reachable from CANDIDATE, MATURED and QUARANTINED, not only ACTIVE. | An antibody that fails maturation or refinement must be closable. |

[project]
name = "kintsugi-omega"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "KINTSUGI-Ω (Blueprint Omega): an immune system for a fleet of AI agents. #neatHack 2026."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"
authors = [{ name = "Surya Prasanth R", email = "suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com" }]
license = { text = "Proprietary — #neatHack 2026 submission" }
dependencies = [
    "cryptography>=44.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.23",
    "networkx>=3.4",
    "numpy>=2.1",
    "pydantic>=2.9",
    "pyrage>=1.2",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.2",
    "rfc8785>=0.1.4",
    "scipy>=1.14",
]

[project.scripts]
kintsugi = "kintsugi.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "hypothesis>=6.120",
    "pyright[nodejs]>=1.1.390",
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "ruff>=0.9",
    "types-jsonschema>=4.23",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.25"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["kintsugi"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"schemas" = "kintsugi/_schemas"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = [".claude", ".entire"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["B", "C4", "E", "F", "I", "PIE", "PT", "RUF", "SIM", "TID", "UP", "W"]
# Spec notation (Ω, σ, τ, φ, ×, ‖, en/em dashes) is intentional, not a confusable.
allowed-confusables = ["×", "‖", "–", "—", "−", "′", "″", "Ω", "α", "β", "δ", "κ", "λ", "σ", "τ", "φ", "ψ", "ι", "ρ", "∗"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["kintsugi"]

# Every child process goes through kintsugi.sandbox.proc (docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md §2d).
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"subprocess".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc: the single gateway (ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0, env allowlist, tree kill)."
"os.system".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc.run."
"os.popen".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc.run."
"asyncio.create_subprocess_exec".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc."
"asyncio.create_subprocess_shell".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["kintsugi", "tests"]
exclude = ["tests/fixtures"]  # fixture repos import their own packages (ledger.*, scout.*)
pythonVersion = "3.12"
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
stubPath = "typings"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --import-mode=importlib"
markers = [
    "contract: needs local Entire or Claude Code tooling (Stage 2+)",
    "slow: long-running",
]
# KINTSUGI-Ω developer and judge entry points (spec §12).
# Every recipe runs with ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 so Entire's git hooks never block on a hidden prompt.

UV ?= uv
export ENTIRE_TEST_TTY := 0
export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT := 0

.PHONY: help sync lint format typecheck test check judge audit demo fleet-up fleet-down

help:
	@echo "sync        install the locked environment"
	@echo "check       lint + typecheck + test (what CI runs)"
	@echo "judge       offline audit of published bundles; needs no credentials (spec §7.5)"
	@echo "audit       online audit of the whole window"
	@echo "demo        run the recorded demo scenario"
	@echo "fleet-up    start the host fleet and the crew"
	@echo "fleet-down  stop the host fleet and the crew"

sync:
	$(UV) sync --locked

lint:
	$(UV) run ruff check .
	$(UV) run ruff format --check .

format:
	$(UV) run ruff format .
	$(UV) run ruff check --fix .

typecheck:
	$(UV) run pyright

test:
	$(UV) run pytest

check: lint typecheck test

judge:
	$(UV) run kintsugi audit --all --offline ./published-bundles

audit:
	$(UV) run kintsugi audit --all

demo:
	$(UV) run kintsugi demo

fleet-up:
	$(UV) run kintsugi fleet up

fleet-down:
	$(UV) run kintsugi fleet down

[project]
name = "kintsugi-omega"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "KINTSUGI-Ω (Blueprint Omega): an immune system for a fleet of AI agents. #neatHack 2026."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12,<3.13"
authors = [{ name = "Surya Prasanth R", email = "suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com" }]
license = { text = "Proprietary — #neatHack 2026 submission" }
dependencies = [
    "cryptography>=44.0",
    "jsonschema>=4.23",
    "networkx>=3.4",
    "numpy>=2.1",
    "pydantic>=2.9",
    "pyrage>=1.2",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.2",
    "rfc8785>=0.1.4",
    "scipy>=1.14",
]

[project.scripts]
kintsugi = "kintsugi.cli:main"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "hypothesis>=6.120",
    "pyright[nodejs]>=1.1.390",
    "pytest>=8.3",
    "ruff>=0.9",
    "types-jsonschema>=4.23",
    "types-pyyaml>=6.0.12",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling>=1.25"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["kintsugi"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"schemas" = "kintsugi/_schemas"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py312"
extend-exclude = [".claude", ".entire"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["B", "C4", "E", "F", "I", "PIE", "PT", "RUF", "SIM", "TID", "UP", "W"]
# Spec notation (Ω, σ, τ, φ, ×, ‖, en/em dashes) is intentional, not a confusable.
allowed-confusables = ["×", "‖", "–", "—", "−", "′", "″", "Ω", "α", "β", "δ", "κ", "λ", "σ", "τ", "φ", "ψ", "ι", "ρ", "∗"]

[tool.ruff.lint.isort]
known-first-party = ["kintsugi"]

# Every child process goes through kintsugi.sandbox.proc (docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md §2d).
[tool.ruff.lint.flake8-tidy-imports.banned-api]
"subprocess".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc: the single gateway (ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0, env allowlist, tree kill)."
"os.system".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc.run."
"os.popen".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc.run."
"asyncio.create_subprocess_exec".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc."
"asyncio.create_subprocess_shell".msg = "Use kintsugi.sandbox.proc."

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py" = ["TID251"]

[tool.pyright]
include = ["kintsugi", "tests"]
exclude = ["tests/fixtures"]  # fixture repos import their own packages (ledger.*, scout.*)
pythonVersion = "3.12"
typeCheckingMode = "standard"
reportMissingTypeStubs = false
stubPath = "typings"
venvPath = "."
venv = ".venv"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["."]
addopts = "-ra --strict-markers --import-mode=importlib"
markers = [
    "contract: needs local Entire or Claude Code tooling (Stage 2+)",
    "slow: long-running",
]
# KINTSUGI-Ω developer and judge entry points (spec §12).
# Every recipe runs with ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0 so Entire's git hooks never block on a hidden prompt.

UV ?= uv
export ENTIRE_TEST_TTY := 0
export GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT := 0

.PHONY: help sync lint format typecheck test check judge audit demo fleet-up fleet-down

help:
	@echo "sync        install the locked environment"
	@echo "check       lint + typecheck + test (what CI runs)"
	@echo "judge       offline audit of published bundles; needs no credentials (spec §7.5)"
	@echo "audit       online audit of the whole window"
	@echo "demo        run the recorded demo scenario"
	@echo "fleet-up    start the host fleet and the crew"
	@echo "fleet-down  stop the host fleet and the crew"

sync:
	$(UV) sync --locked

lint:
	$(UV) run ruff check .
	$(UV) run ruff format --check .

format:
	$(UV) run ruff format .
	$(UV) run ruff check --fix .

typecheck:
	$(UV) run pyright

test:

check: lint typecheck test

judge:

audit:

demo:
	$(UV) run kintsugi demo

fleet-up:
	$(UV) run kintsugi fleet up

fleet-down:

1	# KINTSUGI‑Ω Execution & Build Plan
2	
3	| Field | Value |
4	|---|---|
5	| Status | **Approved by the Architect** (Surya Prasanth R, @suryaprasanthcse), 2026‑10‑11 |
6	| Specification | `../Blueprint_Omega_Master.md` (v1.0, full version). This plan reconciles it with the verified environment; it does not dilute it. |
7	| Visual archive | `../kintsugi-omega-blueprints/kintsugi-omega-blueprint-img_{1..12}.png` |
8	| Scope | Full Blueprint Omega. No reduced cut. |
9	
10	This file is the in-tree source of truth for every interactive or headless session. Amendments discovered during execution are appended to the **Amendments log** at the end, never edited into the approved text.
11	
12	---
13	
14	## 0. Schedule constraint
15	
16	- Plan approval: 12:27 IST, Oct 11. Submission window closes 23:55 IST, Oct 12 (about 35½ h).
17	- The specification itself estimates about 4 engineer-weeks for the full build (§13.2 R1, "Certain"). The estimate for Stages 1–13 below is 45–50 h of continuous wall-clock work.
18	- The autonomy window W must end by about 19:55 IST Oct 12 to leave about 4 h for reveals, audit, video and submission. Therefore **T0 ≤ 19:55 IST Oct 12 − W**.
19	- W and T0 are decided at the Stage 8 go/no-go gate (ruling D1).
20	
21	## 1. Verified environment baseline (pre-Stage 1)
22	
23	| Area | Verified state |
24	|---|---|
25	| Entire | CLI 0.11.4 and entire-graph v0.4.0 (`no_egress: true`). Checkpoints are per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-2-chars>/<ULID>`, not the legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. No `rewind` command exists. Available: `entire checkpoint explain --json/--transcript`, `entire why <file>:<line> --json`, `entire session resume/stop`. |
26	| Entire behaviour | A mid-turn commit is linked only when the files were edited with Claude Code's Edit/Write tools. Each Stop hook adds a "Finalize transcript" commit, which moves the checkpoint ref. The pre-push hook only pushes refs in its local queue. Built-in redaction blanks secret-looking lines even with zero configured rules. |
27	| Windows | Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` blocks on a hidden `CONIN$` prompt unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`. The Claude desktop app is MSIX-packaged and virtualizes `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` writes, so tooling lives under `~/.local/share` (`UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`). |
28	| Tools present | `claude` 2.1.269 (headless CLI; the desktop app runs 2.1.295), Node, npm, git 2.55. Docker Desktop installed, engine stopped. WSL2 distros Ubuntu and docker-desktop (stopped). |
29	| Tools missing | `temporal`, `gh`, `make` (Windows), `age` CLI (the `pyrage` library replaces it). |
30	| Python | uv-managed CPython 3.12.14, pinned by `.python-version`. |
31	| Commit policy | Sole author and committer: Surya Prasanth R `<suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>`. Never `Co-authored-by:`. Attribution only through `Entire-Checkpoint:` and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |
32	
33	## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation
34	
35	### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3
36	
37	- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
38	- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
39	- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.
40	
41	### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record
42	
43	**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:
44	
45	1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
46	2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
47	3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
48	4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
49	5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
50	6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.
51	
52	**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.
53	
54	### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)
55	
56	Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.
57	
58	- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
59	- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
60	- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
61	- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
62	- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).
63	
64	### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere
65	
66	- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
67	- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
68	- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
69	- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
70	- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.
71	
72	### (e) Further reconciliations
73	
74	1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
75	2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
76	3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
77	4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
78	5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
79	6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.
80	
81	## 3. Architect rulings D1–D8
82	
83	| # | Decision | Ruling |
84	|---|---|---|
85	| D1 | W length and T0 | Deferred to the Stage 8 go/no-go gate, once the C1–C14 mutation checks are green. |
86	| D2 | Runtime platform | Stages 1–2 stay cross-platform through `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py` so local Windows execution works. Prepare WSL2 Ubuntu + Docker/gVisor for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run. |
87	| D3 | Repo layout | Build the hosts (`hosts/ledger`, `hosts/scout`, `hosts/triage`), the antibody library (`antibodies/`) and the sabotage log (`sabotage-log/`) inside the `kintsugi-omega` monorepo first, so `suryaprasanthcse/kintsugi-omega` is self-contained and runnable from a single clone. Remote repo adapters are configurable once the GitHub token is provided. |
88	| D4 | Commit identity | `Surya Prasanth R <suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>` is the sole git author and committer on all commits. Never a bot contributor, never `Co-authored-by:`. Machine origin is proven by Ed25519 signatures (`.kintsugi/attest.pub`), `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |
89	| D5 | Ledger location | An unprotected, append-only `ledger` branch for ledger entries and anchors. |
90	| D6 | Temporal deployment | Implement both the deterministic `sqlite_fsm.py` WAL state machine and the Temporal workflow/activity definitions, using the single-binary Temporal CLI dev server or Docker Compose when started in Stage 5. |
91	| D7 | Headless Claude billing | The existing Claude Code login for Stage 2 headless spikes; `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with a hard daily dollar cap in `kintsugi/sandbox/llm_proxy.py` and `kintsugi/econ/governor.py` from Stage 3/6. |
92	| D8 | Parallel build lanes | Approved where safe, provided every commit is made cleanly with `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, carries a verified `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, and credits lines accurately. |
93	
94	## 4. Stages
95	
96	"Rehearsal" means an unsealed, clearly labelled practice run before T0.
97	
98	### Stage 1 — Foundation and deterministic cores (no credentials)
99	
100	- **Builds:** `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, ruff, pyright, `Makefile` (judge, audit, demo, fleet-up/down, check), `.github/workflows/omega-ci.yml`, `kintsugi/cli.py`, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, `kintsugi/proof/{canonical,ledger,sealed,attest,bundle}.py`, `kintsugi/stats/{mcnemar,sprt,power,holm,wilson,bootstrap}.py`, `kintsugi/econ/{governor,wright}.py`, `kintsugi/memory/{antibody,motif}.py`, `kintsugi/control/states.py`, `schemas/E1–E6`, `.kintsugi/protected_paths.yaml`.
101	- **Commits (~7):** scaffold + plan · proc gateway · proof primitives · stats · econ · memory/motif core · state machine, schemas, protected paths.
102	- **Verified by:** SPRT boundaries 2.890/−2.251, steps +0.6931/−0.0660, accept after 35 clean runs, reject at n=8 (LLR 3.268), accept at n=46 (LLR −2.275); Connor n=34; McNemar b=26, c=1 → p≈2.09e-7; governor reproduces §6.2 (Pool $71.70, Cap/B $12.40) and §6.8 (B $4.83, T1 $2.34, GM 78.6%); Wright fit recovers b; RFC 8785 vectors; ledger tamper detected at the exact seq; commit-reveal and Ed25519 round-trip; property test: every state path terminates. Spike N3 is checked on the first commit.
103	- **Invariants:** model-level I3; I4 formulas; I1/I2/I7 primitives. **Cascade/proof:** SPRT core (L3), L5 math, building blocks for C1, C3, C6.
104	
105	### Stage 2 — Entire, graph, git and attestation layer + headless spikes
106	
107	- **Builds:** `kintsugi/memory/{entire,graph}.py` (every subcommand, JSON adapters, golden fixtures), `kintsugi/sandbox/worktree.py`, `kintsugi/crew/claude_session.py` (`claude -p --output-format stream-json --allowedTools … --settings …`, nonce injection, cost and transcript capture), `kintsugi/proof/{commit,redaction}.py`, `tests/contract/test_entire_*.py`.
108	- **Spikes (contract tests on scratch repos):** A1/N2 (does Entire link a commit made after `claude -p` exits?), N1 (redaction vs nonce/honeytoken/prompt formats), N5 (three concurrent worktrees), A14 (`kill -9` mid-session), N4 (hooks inside worktrees), A9 (snapshot schema).
109	- **Commits:** ~6. **Verified by:** C4/C5 pass on real checkpoints and fail on mutated ones; `entire why` agrees with the trailer mapping; the C6 positive control finds a planted honeytoken.
110	- **Invariants:** I2 machinery; I6 detectability; I5 transcript-scan tooling. **Cascade/proof:** L1 attempt checkpoints, L2 abandoned-session handling, C2–C6.
111

# KINTSUGI‑Ω Execution & Build Plan

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Status | **Approved by the Architect** (Surya Prasanth R, @suryaprasanthcse), 2026‑10‑11 |
| Specification | `../Blueprint_Omega_Master.md` (v1.0, full version). This plan reconciles it with the verified environment; it does not dilute it. |
| Visual archive | `../kintsugi-omega-blueprints/kintsugi-omega-blueprint-img_{1..12}.png` |
| Scope | Full Blueprint Omega. No reduced cut. |

This file is the in-tree source of truth for every interactive or headless session. Amendments discovered during execution are appended to the **Amendments log** at the end, never edited into the approved text.

---

## 0. Schedule constraint

- Plan approval: 12:27 IST, Oct 11. Submission window closes 23:55 IST, Oct 12 (about 35½ h).
- The specification itself estimates about 4 engineer-weeks for the full build (§13.2 R1, "Certain"). The estimate for Stages 1–13 below is 45–50 h of continuous wall-clock work.
- The autonomy window W must end by about 19:55 IST Oct 12 to leave about 4 h for reveals, audit, video and submission. Therefore **T0 ≤ 19:55 IST Oct 12 − W**.
- W and T0 are decided at the Stage 8 go/no-go gate (ruling D1).

## 1. Verified environment baseline (pre-Stage 1)

| Area | Verified state |
|---|---|
| Entire | CLI 0.11.4 and entire-graph v0.4.0 (`no_egress: true`). Checkpoints are per-checkpoint refs `refs/entire/checkpoints/<last-2-chars>/<ULID>`, not the legacy `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. No `rewind` command exists. Available: `entire checkpoint explain --json/--transcript`, `entire why <file>:<line> --json`, `entire session resume/stop`. |
| Entire behaviour | A mid-turn commit is linked only when the files were edited with Claude Code's Edit/Write tools. Each Stop hook adds a "Finalize transcript" commit, which moves the checkpoint ref. The pre-push hook only pushes refs in its local queue. Built-in redaction blanks secret-looking lines even with zero configured rules. |
| Windows | Entire's `prepare-commit-msg` blocks on a hidden `CONIN$` prompt unless `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`. The Claude desktop app is MSIX-packaged and virtualizes `%APPDATA%`/`%LOCALAPPDATA%` writes, so tooling lives under `~/.local/share` (`UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DIR`). |
| Tools present | `claude` 2.1.269 (headless CLI; the desktop app runs 2.1.295), Node, npm, git 2.55. Docker Desktop installed, engine stopped. WSL2 distros Ubuntu and docker-desktop (stopped). |
| Tools missing | `temporal`, `gh`, `make` (Windows), `age` CLI (the `pyrage` library replaces it). |
| Python | uv-managed CPython 3.12.14, pinned by `.python-version`. |
| Commit policy | Sole author and committer: Surya Prasanth R `<suryaprasanthcse@gmail.com>`. Never `Co-authored-by:`. Attribution only through `Entire-Checkpoint:` and `Kintsugi-*` trailers. |

## 2. Spec-to-reality reconciliation

### (a) No `rewind`: L1, L2, L3

- **L1 (failed hypotheses).** Rewind means *discard the worktree, keep the checkpoint* (spec §4.3.4, honest scope). Every attempt therefore commits, including attempts that will fail the gates, because a checkpoint exists only for a commit. The Surgeon session edits `wt/INC/Hk`; after the session ends the orchestrator signs and commits on `kintsugi/INC/Hk`; Entire links the commit to the session. The attempt is pinned as `refs/kintsugi/attempts/INC/Hk/<n>` and pushed with the checkpoint refs; then `git worktree remove --force`. Attempt commits stay reachable (never garbage-collected) and audit checks C2–C5 can verify them.
- **L2 (process killed mid-session).** A headless session killed before its Stop hook has no shadow branch and no checkpoint (A14). Recovery: adopt a commit whose nonce matches the ledger; otherwise kill the process group, `entire session stop <id>`, `git reset --hard` + `git clean -fdx` inside the disposable worktree only, hash the Claude Code transcript (`~/.claude/projects/.../<sid>.jsonl`) into the bundle as evidence of the abandoned attempt, write an `abandoned` ledger entry, and start attempt 2 with a **new nonce**. Long-lived in-place sessions (Immunologist refinement, orphan recovery) use `entire session resume <branch>` plus `claude -p --resume <sid>` (spike N7).
- **L3 (wrong fix in production).** Reverting is git (`git revert -m 1` → PR → expedited gates → merge), not Entire. Because audit check C4 requires a checkpoint for **every** commit in W, reverts, L5 configuration treatments and eval-augment commits run inside a templated **headless notary session**: a Claude Code session whose prompt contains the nonce and performs exactly that operation.

### (b) Audit check C4 and the Archivist's Intent Record

**C4/C5**, for every commit in W on protected branches plus attempt refs:

1. Require both the `Kintsugi-*` trailers and an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
2. The ref `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` must exist on origin. Offline mode reads a `git bundle` of these refs.
3. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json`: `files_touched` must cover the files in the diff.
4. `entire checkpoint explain <id> --transcript`: the nonce must appear verbatim and not on a redacted line.
5. Cross-check: `entire why <file>:<line> --json` on sampled changed lines names the same checkpoint and commit.
6. **C5:** the session's first user message, canonicalised and SHA-256'd, equals `Kintsugi-Prompt`.

**Intent Record:** `entire graph search` → `git blame` → resolve the checkpoint two independent ways (`entire why --json` and the commit trailer; they must agree) → read the transcript → select the turn(s) whose Edit/Write tool calls touched the blamed file (the "Intent" field is ignored: it shows the first prompt in the checkpoint's scope) → the Archivist (Opus) writes clauses with verbatim quotes → the Auditor checks every quote against the same transcript bytes, whose SHA-256 is recorded. `git bisect` steps map to checkpoints through trailers; commits without one are labelled `no-checkpoint`. The honeytoken check (§7.2) runs `git grep` over **all** `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` trees.

### (c) Motif engine on entire-graph v0.4.0 (Python)

Python relations: `CALLS`, `ASYNC_CALLS`, `CONSTRUCTS`, `CONTAINS`, `DATA_FLOWS`, `DEFINES`, `IMPORTS`, `EXTENDS`, `INHERITS`, `OVERRIDES`, `PARAM_TYPE`, `RETURNS_TYPE`, `USES_TYPE`, `HANDLES_GRAPHQL`, plus the heuristic relations of the `full` profile (`HTTP_CALLS`, `HANDLES_TOOL`, `TESTS`, `FILE_CHANGES_WITH`). There is no `READS_FIELD`, `WRITES_FIELD`, `ACCESSES` or `IMPLEMENTS` for Python.

- **Motif v1.0:** nodes `R[is_retry_wrapper]`, `Enc` (enclosing function), `F` (the retried scope: nested function, lambda, or the decorated function itself), `S[has_mutable_accumulator]`; edges `[Enc,R,CALLS]`, `[Enc,F,CONTAINS]`, **`[F,S,CONSTRUCTS]`**.
- **Motif v1.1** adds `T[is_side_effecting]` and `[F,T,CALLS*]`, where `CALLS*` is a derived transitive-closure relation computed before VF2 matching (VF2 matches edges exactly).
- **`has_mutable_accumulator`:** `entire graph def S` (fields and methods) plus a deterministic stdlib `ast` scan for list/dict/set fields mutated in methods; Haiku decides only when the scan is inconclusive, and its verdict is cached by (symbol, blob SHA).
- **`is_side_effecting`:** `CALLS*` reaches a tool annotated `side_effect: true` in the host's tool registry, or an `HTTP_CALLS` POST/PUT/DELETE.
- Validation is unchanged: match before the fix, no match after it, precision ≥ 0.9 on the healthy fleet. The snapshot record schema is pinned with golden files (A9).

### (d) `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0` everywhere

- Build commits: `.claude/settings.json` `env` block and the CLAUDE.md commit rules.
- Runtime: one subprocess gateway, `kintsugi/sandbox/proc.py`, builds every child environment from an allowlist and forces `ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_EDITOR=true`, with timeouts and process-tree termination (root first, so a killed `git commit` aborts instead of completing without a trailer). An architecture test and a ruff banned-API rule forbid `subprocess` anywhere else.
- Headless sessions get the environment from the gateway plus `--settings` (which also sets commit attribution to `""`).
- Every commit is verified afterwards (trailer + checkpoint ref). On failure the activity fails, the disposable worktree is reset and nothing is pushed.
- Entire 0.11.4 and entire-graph 0.4.0 are pinned; a contract test runs the hook on a scratch repo under a timeout to catch regressions.

### (e) Further reconciliations

1. **Redaction vs. the proofs (critical, spike N1).** Entire redacts secret-looking lines. A hex nonce or random-looking honeytoken could be blanked: C4 would fail and, worse, C6's "0 honeytoken hits" would pass trivially. Nonces and honeytokens are therefore **passphrase-formatted**; Stage 2 adds a byte-exact prompt round-trip test and a **positive control** proving C6 finds a planted honeytoken.
2. **Parallel Surgeons (N5).** K concurrent sessions in K worktrees: each commit must link to its own session.
3. **Ref syncing.** Checkpoint refs are pushed explicitly after each commit and again after finalize; audit clones fetch `refs/entire/*`.
4. **Public transcripts.** Checkpoint transcripts are pushed with the code: add redaction rules for Anthropic and neatlogs key patterns and a secret scan of checkpoint trees before every push (N6).
5. **Platform.** gVisor (§5.10) needs Linux: the runtime for Stage 3+ and the autonomy run lives in WSL2 Ubuntu (ruling D2). The 24 h run is never launched from inside the Claude desktop app.
6. **No co-author trailers.** The orchestrator's commit validator rejects `Co-authored-by:`; headless sessions get commit attribution set to `""`.

definition.name: mcp__aws-mcp__aws___run_script
definition.description:
Execute Python code in sandboxed environment with AWS API access via `call_boto3`. No network except `call_boto3`.

```python
async def call_boto3(
    *,
    service_name: str,
    operation_name: str,
    region_name: str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
) -> dict: ...
```

``operation_name`` MUST be the PascalCase AWS API operation name (e.g. ``ListBuckets``,
``GetTable``, ``StartQueryExecution``). Do not use the snake_case boto3 method name
(``list_buckets``, ``get_table``); exact matches are corrected only as a runtime fallback.

### 4.1 neatlogs as the afferent system (senses) #### 4.1.1 Instrumenting the hosts [V] Every host is instrumented with the neatlogs Python SDK. It requires Python ≥3.10 and <3.14. Install the extras for the libraries the host uses, for example `neatlogs[anthropic]`. ```python import os import neatlogs neatlogs.init( api_key=os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"], # or the NEATLOGS_API_KEY env var workflow_name=f"host:{HOST_ID}", # naming convention, see §4.1.3 instrumentations=["anthropic"], # add "openai", "langchain", "crewai", "mcp" as detected ) # Import order rule [V]: instrumented libraries MUST be imported AFTER init(). import anthropic from neatlogs import span @span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="reconcile_invoice") def run_task(task): ... # Scripts MUST call neatlogs.flush() and then neatlogs.shutdown() at exit. # Servers call init() once and never shut down per request. ``` - **Diagnostics [V]:** - `python -m neatlogs doctor --local --json` makes no network calls. - `neatlogs doctor --probe --json` exports and reads back one trace. It requires `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`. - **Optional env vars [V]:** `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` (default `https://ingest.neatlogs.com`) and `NEATLOGS_UPLOADS_ENABLED`. - **Span kinds.** The portal's example trace shows `agent`, `llm` and `tool` spans [V, portal screenshot]. The SDK README documents `WORKFLOW` explicitly. The full set of kind values is [A] (spike A7). - **Grader spans.** Every host's eval runner MUST emit a dedicated span `grader.verdict` with output `PASS` or `FAIL:`, so regex receptors can match it. #### 4.1.2 Instrumenting the crew - Every crew role runs with `workflow_name = "kintsugi:"`. - Each incident's root span is a `WORKFLOW` span named `incident:`. - All crew traces for one incident share the session id `inc-` [A: session id set through the SDK's `trace()` helper; spike A3]. That makes `GET /traces?sessionId=inc-0042` [V] and `GET /sessions/{sessionId}/export` [V] return the full cost ledger of the incident. #### 4.1.3 Trace tag schema `PATCH /traces/{traceId}` accepts `tags` (at most 10, each 1–128 characters) and requires `expectedRevision` for optimistic concurrency [V]. Omega writes tags read-modify-write and retries on a revision conflict. | Tag | Values | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `host:` | `ledger`, `scout`, `triage`, `clinic-a`, … | Fleet partitioning | | `inc:` | `INC-0042` | Incident linkage | | `phase:

` | `baseline` `repro` `before` `after` `canary` `vacc` `sabotage` `selfrepair` | Before/after evidence | | `hyp:` | `H1`…`Hk` | Hypothesis identity | | `ab:` | `AB-17@1.1` | Antibody version applied | | `split:` | `train` `hold` | Eval split (task content is never in tags) | | `seed:` | integer | Reproducibility | | `gate:` | `G4-pass`, `G3-fail` | Verdict linkage | | `run:` | 8-char run id | Grouping | #### 4.1.4 Innate receptors (baseline detections on every host) ===== ### 5.9 The fleet #### 5.9.1 Ledger (ours): invoice-to-ledger reconciliation | Field | Specification | |---|---| | Tools | `parse_invoice` (text/PDF → structured), `lookup_vendor` (vendor master), `fx_rate` (external FX API through the chaos proxy), **`post_journal_entry` (side-effecting: writes to the ledger DB)**, `reconcile_report` | | Eval | 120 synthetic invoices [I] generated with seeds: multi-currency, multi-page, credit notes, partial payments. 80 train / 40 holdout. | | Grader | Exact journal-line match (account, amount to the cent, currency, date); duplicates and missing lines are failures | | SLO | ≥ 90% pass, p95 ≤ 25 s [I] | | v_h, λ_h | $3.00 per failed task; 40 tasks per hour (traffic generator) [I] | | Model | `claude-haiku-5-5` by default; the cfo.ai cost scenario drives the tier choice | #### 5.9.2 Scout (ours): research with citations | Field | Specification | |---|---| | Tools | `web_search` over a **frozen local corpus** (BM25) to remove internet variance; `fetch_document`; `verify_citations` | | Eval | 60 questions with gold answers and gold citation sets [I]; 40 train / 20 holdout | | Grader | Answer correctness (neatlogs evaluator with a rubric) plus citation precision and recall; **duplicate citations are failures** | | SLO | ≥ 85% [I] | | Design note | Scout constructs a per-attempt scratch buffer inside its retry wrapper. **Per-attempt reset is intended**, because its retried scope has no external side effects. This look-alike pattern is deliberately present and disclosed, to test the L3 response (§6.7). | #### 5.9.3 Triage (ours): GitHub issue triage on a frozen snapshot | Field | Specification | |---|---| | Tools | `search_issues` (local index), `get_issue`, `apply_label` (side-effecting, on a mock GitHub), `comment` (mock); optional Crustdata enrichment of the reporter's organisation | | Eval | 100 issues with gold labels, duplicates and routes [I]; 70 / 30 split | | SLO | ≥ 88% [I] | | Commercial tier in the model | **Pilot** ($99 per month), used for the L5 economics demonstration | #### 5.9.4 Onboarding pipeline (Clinic and OSS hosts, zero configuration) | Step | Action | |---|---| | O1 Intake | Repo URL, entry point, run command, model provider, consent (§7.6) | | O2 Sandbox | Clone into a gVisor or Fargate sandbox; dependency install with egress allowlist | | O3 Instrument | Headless Claude Code following the neatlogs-py skill rules (init before imports; instrumentations detected from imports) on a **local branch only**; `neatlogs doctor --local --json` must pass | | O4 Entire | `entire enable`; `entire graph init-agents`; `entire graph index`; `entire graph snapshot` | | O5 Eval synthesis | Build tasks from README examples, existing tests and docstrings. Graders: deterministic where possible, otherwise a neatlogs evaluator with a rubric. Split train/holdout; commit the holdout manifest hash. | | O6 Baseline | 3 seeds over the eval set; health card (pass rate with Wilson CI, cost, p95) | | O7 Immune scan | Match every ACTIVE antibody motif against `G_h`; queue vaccinations | If the host needs third-party API keys that cannot be provided, Omega uses **replay mode**: cassettes are built from the owner's exported neatlogs traces (`GET /traces/{id}/export` on their project, shared by them), so tool I/O is replayed without keys. ### 5.10 Sandboxing and security | Control | Specification | |---|---| | Isolation | gVisor (`runsc`) locally; Fargate (Firecracker) hosted. Non-root user, read-only root filesystem, tmpfs workdir, limits on CPU, memory, PIDs and wall-clock time. | | Secrets | **No secrets inside sandboxes.** The LLM API key lives only in the **LLM metering proxy** outside the sandbox. The proxy injects credentials, enforces per-host budgets and records cost per host for the actuals pipeline. | | Egress | Allowlist: the LLM proxy, `ingest.neatlogs.com`, the package mirror during install only. Everything else is denied. | | Chaos proxy | All host tool calls to "external" services go through a seeded chaos proxy (latency, 429s, schema drift, partial responses). Its configuration is sealed by the Saboteur. | | Prompt injection | Host data (invoices, issues, documents) is treated as untrusted. Crew roles never execute instructions found in host data. The Arena only accepts catalog parameters (§7.7). | | Clinic code | Untrusted by default. Omega never runs it outside the sandbox and never auto-merges into a foreign repo. | ### 5.11 Verification fabric: gates G0–G7 and the canary | Gate | Name | Check | Tooling | Pass criterion | On failure | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **G0** | Reproduction | Replay the cassette before the fix | Cassette runner | **Fails 3/3 seeds** | Widen the cassette (×3), then PARK: no reproduction, no repair | | **G1** | Build and static | Install, lint, type-check | `uv sync`, `ruff`, `pyright` | Exit 0 | Discard the hypothesis | | **G2** | Reproduction fixed | Replay the cassette after the fix | Cassette runner | **Passes 3/3 seeds** | Rewind; feed back the replay diff | | **G3** | No collateral damage | Test state changes | `entire graph verify --test "pytest -q" --pre-edit-baseline` | **Zero pass→fail flips** | Rewind; feed back the list of flipped tests | | **G4** | Held-out efficacy | Paired evaluation on the encrypted holdout | Eval runner + neatlogs tags + stats | Exact McNemar one-sided p < 0.05 (Holm-corrected across hosts in a wave) **and** the cost Δ upper bound < +5% **and** the p95 Δ upper bound < +10% | Rewind; feed back aggregates only (never task content) | | **G5** | Intent fidelity | Patch vs Intent Record | Auditor (Opus) with verbatim-quote check | No contract clause violated | Rank the hypothesis down, or reject it | | **G6** | Budget | Cumulative incident spend | Governor | ≤ B_ι | Stop the round → cheaper treatment or ESCALATE | | **G7** | Independent CI | G1–G4 re-run in GitHub Actions with a **fresh seed** | Actions (public logs) | All pass | Block the merge | | **C** | Canary | Live-traffic SPRT after the merge | neatlogs grader spans + SPRT | Accept H0 (no regression) | Auto-revert → quarantine → re-enter REPAIRING | **Anti-gaming rules:** - Protected paths are enforced twice: a pre-commit hook in each worktree, and an Auditor diff check. - Diff budget: ≤ 120 changed lines by default [I]. A larger diff needs Coordinator approval, which is recorded. - No new outbound network calls may appear in a diff; this is checked with `entire graph diff` plus a pattern scan. - Holdout tasks are encrypted at rest with age. The decryption key is available only inside the Auditor's G4 activity. The manifest hash is committed at T0. - Surgeons receive only aggregate G4 feedback: Δpass, the confidence interval and the cost Δ. ### 5.12 Statistics **Paired efficacy (G4).** For each holdout task and seed pair (before, after): - b = number of pairs that failed before and passed after; Shell cwd was reset to C:\myspace\hacckathons\kintsugi-omega

#### 4.1.4 Innate receptors (baseline detections on every host)

Detections come in four types [V]:
- **regex** on span input or output;
- **condition** on numeric or boolean attributes, e.g. token counts, latency, cost or `tool_call_count`;
- **PII**;
- **classifier** (semantic).

| ID | Type | Rule | Catches |
|---|---|---|---|
| R‑001 | regex | Tool span output matches `(?i)(traceback\|exception\|HTTP\s?(4\d\d\|5\d\d)\|"status":\s*"error")` | Tool and HTTP failures |
| R‑002 | condition | `tool_call_count > 10` (the documented loop example [V]) | Runaway loops |
| R‑003 | condition | Trace cost > `c_max_h` | Cost blow-ups |
| R‑004 | condition | Trace latency > `l_max_h` | Latency regressions |
| R‑005 | classifier | Output is off-task or does not match the retrieved evidence | Semantic failures |
| R‑006 | PII | PII present in outputs | Privacy leaks. Ledger handles vendor bank data, so the fixtures are synthetic. |
| R‑007 | regex | `grader.verdict` output matches `^FAIL:` | Correctness failures |

Each receptor is attached to an alert rule, for example "≥3 hits in 10 minutes per host", which fires a webhook. Alert rules can be **listed** through the API (`GET /alert-rules`, `GET /alert-history`) [V]. **Creating** them through the API is [A], so they are configured in the UI on Day 0 (spike A13).
